title: Finite-type saturation under a fibrewise neutral open subgroup
statement: Let $S$ be an affine Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $G\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme, locally of finite type [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the group diagrams (the relative form of [def-sc-group-scheme]); separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $H\subseteq G$ be an open subgroup scheme of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$, $H_{\bar s}$ is the connected component containing the identity in $G_{\bar s}$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $W\subseteq G$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme (its underlying space is quasi-compact). Define $|X|$ to be the image on underlying points of the multiplication morphism $H\times_SW\to G$. Then $|X|$ is open, contains $|W|$, and its open subscheme $X\subseteq G$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $S$. Multiplication restricts to an action $H\times_SX\to X$. For every geometric point $\bar s$, $X_{\bar s}$ is a union of connected components of $G_{\bar s}$, and each nonempty such component is a single orbit of $H_{\bar s}$: for any algebraically closed extension $\Omega$ of its residue field and $x,y\in X_{\bar s}(\Omega)$ in that component there is $h\in H_{\bar s}(\Omega)$ with $hx=y$.

source.place: BLR 6.6 Theorem 2, introductory image construction and proof of (a), printed pp.164–165 (PDF pp.170–171); 6.4 discussion of the identity component before Lemma 3, printed pp.154–155; 10.1 discussion after Definition 1, printed p.290. Scheme-only saturation lemma extracted from these arguments; no Néron mapping property assumed. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: Restrict $G\to S$ to $H$; this is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Thus $p_2:H\times_SG\to G$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The morphism $\alpha(h,g)=(h,hg)$ is an automorphism of $H\times_SG$, with inverse $(h,g)\mapsto(h,h^{-1}g)$: these identities are precisely the group inverse and associativity diagrams. The action $a(h,g)=hg$ equals $p_2\alpha$, so is smooth by the isomorphism clause of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Its restriction $b:H\times_SW\to G$ is smooth by the open-restriction clause of the same node. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $b$ is open. In particular its image $|X|$ is open.

source.place: Tags 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 01UA (lemma-fppf-open); BLR 6.6 Theorem 2 proof, printed p.164, action as an automorphism followed by a projection

proof.text: The finite-type hypothesis on $H\to S$ implies that it is quasi-compact. By [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], $H\times_SW\to W$ is quasi-compact. Its inverse image of the quasi-compact open $W$ is the whole source, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open] makes $H\times_SW$ quasi-compact. The continuous-image assertion [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact] makes $|X|$ quasi-compact. Give it its open-subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tags 01K5 (lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change), 01K4 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine); topology.tex Tag 04Z9 (lemma-image-quasi-compact); BLR 6.6 Theorem 2(a), printed p.165, quasi-compact multiplication source

proof.text: The open subscheme $X$ is smooth over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], and separated over $S$ by [lem-trf-immersion-over-separated-base]. Smoothness gives local finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. In an affine presentation $A=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], the classes of the $t_i$ generate $A$ as an $R$-algebra, so the morphism is locally of finite type. Finally $S$ is affine and hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $X$ is quasi-compact by step 2, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $X\to S$ quasi-compact. Together these give finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize); schemes.tex Tag 01L8 (lemma-subscheme-of-separated-scheme), Tag 01K4 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine); definition of finite type, Tag 01T0

proof.text: The section $w\mapsto(e,w)$ of $H\times_SW\to W$ has composite $w\mapsto w$ in $G$, so $W\subseteq X$. We check the image of $H\times_SX\to G$ lies in $X$. Take any point $z$ of $H\times_SX$, and use its residue field $K$ to obtain $h\in H(K)$ and $x\in X(K)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image], the fibre of $b$ over this $K$-point $x$ is nonempty. Choose a point of that fibre, with residue field $L$; it gives $a\in H(L)$ and $w\in W(L)$ with $x_L=aw$. The group law gives $h_Lx_L=(h_La)w$, which is in the image of $b$. Its underlying point is the image of $z$, so this image lies in $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] the multiplication therefore factors uniquely through $X$. Associativity and the unit identity hold after the inclusion $X\hookrightarrow G$, and uniqueness in that same node makes them hold in $X$. This is the claimed action.

source.place: Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective), subset-image formula from Tag 0495; schemes.tex Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens); group diagrams

proof.text: Fix a geometric point with algebraically closed field $k$, and put $F=G_k$, $C=H_k$. By smooth base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change], $F$ is smooth and locally of finite type. By hypothesis $C=F^0$. The node [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] says that $C$ is open and closed, connected and geometrically irreducible, and that this identity component commutes with field extension. Every connected component $D$ of $F$ is closed. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], it contains a closed point of $F$, rational over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]; call it $g$. Right translation $r_g$ is an automorphism with inverse $r_{g^{-1}}$, by the group diagrams. Hence $r_g(C)$ is connected, open and closed, and contains $g$. It is contained in $D$ by maximal connectedness, and equals $D$ since a nonempty clopen subset of a connected space is the whole space. Thus $r_g:C\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ is an isomorphism of open subschemes. This uses no finiteness of the number of components of $F$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component); varieties.tex Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson); morphisms.tex Tag 01TB (lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points). Translation argument written out; BLR 6.4 discussion before Lemma 3, printed pp.154–155

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image], $X_k$ is exactly the image of $H_k\times_kW_k\to G_k$; in particular it is the base change of the open constructed above. If a component $D$ of $F$ meets $X_k$, then $D\cap X_k$ is a nonempty open subscheme of the smooth $k$-scheme $F$, by step 5. It is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], so [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] supplies $w\in(D\cap X_k)(k)$. Repeating the translation argument of step 5 with this $w$ gives $D=Cw$. The action of step 4 shows $Cw\subseteq X_k$ (base-change the factorization using [def-pc-base-change]). Consequently every component meeting $X_k$ is wholly contained in it: $X_k$ is a union of connected components of $F$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R and translation by a rational point; BLR 6.4 discussion before Lemma 3, printed pp.154–155, identity-component orbits on geometric fibres

proof.text: For a component $D\subseteq X_k$, choose $w\in D(k)$ as in step 6. The isomorphism $C\xrightarrow{h\mapsto hw}D$ base changes to an isomorphism $C_\Omega\xrightarrow{\sim}D_\Omega$ for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, by the fibre-product definition [def-pc-base-change]. The field-extension clause of [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] identifies $C_\Omega$ with the identity component of $F_\Omega$, so $D_\Omega$ is connected as well. Given $x,y\in D(\Omega)$, write uniquely $x=aw$, $y=bw$ with $a,b\in C(\Omega)$. Then $h=ba^{-1}\in C(\Omega)=H_k(\Omega)$ satisfies $hx=ba^{-1}aw=bw=y$. This is the asserted orbit statement, including its extension-field quantifier. If $W$ is empty, all constructions yield the empty $X$ and there is no component to consider.

I read all 7 steps against the statements of the 20 cited nodes and they hold. (1) a(h,g)=hg equals p2∘α, with α(h,g)=(h,hg) an automorphism. Smoothness comes from restrict-open (a)/(b)/(c) and smooth base change. Flat + lfp makes b open. (2) Quasi-compactness uses only H of finite type, through qc base change and the image of a qc space. (3) Smooth, separated (immersion followed by separated) and finite type, using S affine ⇒ qs and permanence (1); the lfp⇒lft step is standard locality (a Mathlib instance), accepted as elementary. (4) Stability uses the base-change-image node to get an L-point x_L=aw, then h_L·a·w, the open factorization, and the action identities by uniqueness. (5) A component D has a closed, k-rational point g (Jacobson + closed-point residue field), and r_g(C)=D by the clopen argument, with no assumption of finitely many components. (6) A rational w ∈ D∩X_k comes from lem-pc-rational-points-dense (alg. closed ⇒ separably closed), and Cw ⊆ X_k comes from the base-changed action. (7) x=aw, y=bw, h=ba⁻¹, keeping the Ω quantifier.
